title: D-GAP K-Means: Selecting and Updating Cluster Centers Without a Prespecified Outlier Count
content: Outliers can compromise \(k\)-means both during initialization and subsequent mean updates. Density-Gap-Aware Protected K-Means (D-GAP K-Means) addresses these two failure points without asking the user how many outliers are present. It first estimates how crowded each observation's neighborhood is and looks for a clear break between sparse observations and the main data. It then chooses initial centers from the retained observations and calculates subsequent centers from those observations only, while still assigning every observation a cluster label. The procedure reports a warning when no clear primary break is found. Conditional on separated hard-ball inliers, locally sparse outlier neighborhoods, a dominant significant primary jump, and refinement preservation, D-GAP-R\(^\star\) is classical \(k\)-means++ on the recovered inliers and therefore inherits its \(8(\ln k+2)\) expected SSE bound. On a 19-cell development suite, D-GAP-Pro attains mean adjusted Rand index (ARI) 0.851 versus 0.770 for an Isolation-Forest pipeline, but the all-pair Holm-adjusted value is \(p=0.069\). A post-freeze 56-cell synthetic holdout reverses the means (0.832 versus 0.860) because D-GAP-Pro fails on dense outlier clumps. In a separate audit over nine real-feature dataset bases, D-GAP-Pro and Isolation Forest attain base-mean ARI 0.541 and 0.505; their mean difference is 0.036 (bootstrap 95% CI [\(-0.034\), 0.115]; 5/0/4 wins/ties/losses). Thus the new evidence establishes competitiveness rather than superiority. The results support a diagnosable method for density-gap regimes, not a generally dominant robust clustering procedure.
